subject: Mutual action plan + perf evaluation summary / quantization kernel notes
messages:
From: Claire Reeves <claire@ignite.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps — perf MAP and quant benchmarks

Hi Vivek / Monica —

Thanks again for the demo. As discussed on the call, Ignite needs a short mutual action plan (MAP) that encodes performance acceptance criteria and a clear close timeline. Primary asks from our side:

- Confirm TTFT and steady-state latency SLO we can expect for a 2B decoder-only model at sequence lengths 256/512.
- Benchmark matrix that compares FP16/BF16 vs INT8 and INT4 for throughput (tokens/sec), median latency, and first-token time (TTFT).
- Concurrency profile for up to 32 concurrent requests with 8/16 token generation variability.
- Regression checks to ensure no token-generation quality regressions when moving to INT8/INT4; provide simple eval harness and CI trigger.

We ran a quick internal smoke test and attached our raw run (perf_results_ignite_run-20261118.csv) — results look noisy; would prefer Redwood’s engineered runtime numbers and kernel-level notes (which kernels were swapped/quantized).

Can you send a MAP with owners/timing by EOD Thursday (2026-11-19) and a short results pack after your perf run? We’re targeting contract signature by 2026-12-03 if the numbers align.

Claire
Head of Platform, Ignite.ai

Attachments referenced: ignite_smoke_20261118.csv (we uploaded to shared drive)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reeves <claire@ignite.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Next steps — perf MAP and quant benchmarks

Claire —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a first-draft MAP and a short plan for the perf matrix. High-level bullets:

1) MAP milestones (owner / deliverable / target)
   - 2026-11-19: Redwood publishes perf evaluation plan + measurement harness (Owner: Marcus)
   - 2026-11-21: Customer-run reproducibility checklist + smoke results (Owner: Claire)
   - 2026-11-24: Redwood delivers kernel profile + quant results (Owner: Marcus)
   - 2026-11-30: Joint QA run & regression pass (Owner: Monica)
   - 2026-12-03: Final exec sign-off (commercial) / PO issued (Owner: Vivek)

2) Acceptance criteria (proposal)
   - TTFT (first-token time) <= 40ms median @ seq=256, <= 65ms @ seq=512 for single-request median on dedicated instance class c8-gpu-32 (Redwood Dedicated).
   - Steady-state token latency (p50/p95) and throughput targets will be provided per model variant; baseline FP16 target: p50 <= 8ms/token at batch size 1.
   - INT8 target: throughput >= 1.8x FP16 baseline with <= 3% perplexity delta on eval set. INT4 flagged as experimental; require regression gating.

3) Measurement harness
   - We'll provide a containerized harness (HTTP + KV prefix caching disabled for baseline runs) and a per-iteration trace to capture kernel-level timings and GPU occupancy.

I’ve attached Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx with owners and the perf script. Marcus — can you run the quant/kernel profile against Ignite’s sample workload (they provided seed prompts) and upload results by Friday morning?

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Solutions & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Reeves <claire@ignite.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T07:28:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Next steps — perf MAP and quant benchmarks — initial run results

Team / Claire —

I ran the Redwood perf harness against Ignite’s seed prompts on a c8-gpu-32 instance. Quick summary (attached CSV + PDF):

- Setup: 2B decoder-only model, beamless sampling, baseline FP16 and BF16 runs, then INT8 (symmetric per-channel) and INT4 (4-bit asymmetric) quantized builds using Redwood runtime quant path. KV prefix caching disabled for fair comparison.

Key numbers (median across 500 samples, seq=256 unless noted):
- FP16 (baseline): throughput 1,200 tokens/sec, TTFT median 35ms, token p50 7.1ms, p95 18.5ms
- BF16: throughput 1,150 tokens/sec, TTFT 36ms, token p50 7.4ms, p95 19.0ms
- INT8: throughput 2,150 tokens/sec, TTFT 45ms, token p50 4.0ms, p95 11.2ms (1.79x throughput vs FP16)
- INT4: throughput 2,900 tokens/sec, TTFT 82ms, token p50 2.8ms, p95 9.6ms (note higher TTFT due to extra per-request dequantization kernel)

Concurrency profile (seq=256, tokens/sec aggregate):
- 1 concurrent: FP16 1,200 t/s; INT8 2,150 t/s; INT4 2,900 t/s
- 8 concurrent: FP16 9k t/s aggregate (p50 per-request ~10ms); INT8 15.8k t/s; INT4 19.7k t/s
- 32 concurrent: saturation point seen for INT4 at ~21.2k t/s with rising tail-latency (p95 > 120ms) due to memory-bandwidth kernel contention on the dequant path.

Regression checks (automatic eval harness, 3 small prompt suites):
- INT8: average perplexity delta +1.7% vs FP16, Rouge-L delta within expected band; pass
- INT4: average perplexity delta +6.9% and several samples with hallucination increase; FAIL gating — recommend INT4 only for non-critical throughput-first workloads after quality sign-off.

Kernel notes (high level):
- INT8 path used optimized fused GEMM + quant-accumulate kernel (kernels qgemm_v2, fast_dequant).
- INT4 introduced an extra dequant step (kernel dequant_batch_v1) that increases TTFT per request — explains higher TTFT even with better steady throughput.
- Observed a regression in a custom fused attention kernel when sequence length > 512 under INT8; falling back to slower attention kernel increased p95 by ~12% in a small subset. We’ll include a patch candidate.

Files attached: perf_results_ignite_run-20261119.csv, quant_kernel_profile-20261119.pdf

Action items:
- Marcus to push a kernel fallback patch and re-run the INT8 seq>512 case (ETA 2026-11-20 noon PT).
- Monica to coordinate a joint QA run 2026-11-24.
- Vivek to keep commercial timeline (target 2026-12-03).

— Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf_results_ignite_run-20261119.csv; quant_kernel_profile-20261119.pdf

From: Claire Reeves <claire@ignite.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:50:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Next steps — perf MAP and quant benchmarks — initial run results

Marcus —

Thanks for the detailed run and the kernel notes. Helpful. A couple quick clarifications before our QA run:

- On TTFT for INT4: can you confirm how much of that 82ms is fixed per-request overhead vs per-token? If the fixed dequant cost is ~40–45ms we might still accept for batch-oriented workloads.
- For the INT8 attention regression at seq>512 — is the proposed patch expected to restore p95 to within 5% of FP16? That’s our gating for production.

We’re happy to run your harness in our enclave on Monday (2026-11-22) to validate reproducibility if you can provide a runbook and container.

Assuming a positive regression pass, we remain on track to finalize PO by 2026-12-03.

Claire

On attachments: we pulled your CSV and PDF and placed a copy in our shared bucket.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reeves <claire@ignite.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Next steps — perf MAP and quant benchmarks — patch run + final notes

Claire / Team —

Quick follow-up after implementing the attention fallback patch and re-running the targeted tests:

Patch result highlights (focused on the seq>512 regression):
- The fallback replaces the fused attention for the pathological path and restores p95 to within 4.2% of FP16 for the affected traces (meets Ignite gating).
- INT8 TTFT remains elevated vs FP16 (median TTFT 48ms) but p50 token times and throughput improved versus prior run.
- INT4 fixed-per-request dequant measured ~42ms on average; per-token remains very low — so INT4 is attractive only when you can amortize the dequant cost across long generations or batch workloads.
- No new regressions introduced by the fallback; kernel-level trace attached.

Next steps / confirmations:
- Marcus: upload final harness container + runbook to the shared drive (done). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ignite/perf/20261120/harness_container.tar.gz
- Claire: please run Redwood harness in your enclave on 2026-11-22 as proposed and share the raw CSVs; Monica will own the QA checklist on 2026-11-24.
- Vivek: commercial team to proceed with draft SOW & PO terms if Ignite confirms run reproducibility (target sign-off 2026-12-03).

I’m marking INT8 as "supported with guarded rollout" in the MAP and INT4 as "experimental: gated by QA & quality sign-off". Full notes and the kernel-profile PDF uploaded (quant_kernel_profile-20261120.pdf).

— Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: quant_kernel_profile-20261120.pdf
